key_insight: Combining histopathology AI, predicted morphological features, and manually assessed PRAME staining showed strong melanoma discrimination but little improvement over AI alone.
clinical_relevance: This diagnostic research—not drug discovery—offers a structured way to combine AI outputs with established pathology findings, without establishing readiness for clinical use.
method: Analyze whole-slide images using the Virchow2 foundation model and STAMP framework.
Predict malignancy and established morphological features from histology.
Combine AI predictions with manually assessed PRAME immunohistochemistry.
evidence_signal: In a retrospective cohort of 1,000 lesions, models trained on 800 cases and tested on 200 temporally held-out cases achieved malignancy AUROCs of 0.970 for AI alone and 0.972 for the integrated model.
watch_item: Performance in this PRAME-tested retrospective cohort requires external and prospective validation before broader clinical implementation.
paper_title: Integrating Histopathology Foundation Models and PRAME Immunohistochemistry in Melanoma Diagnosis
